purpose: Introduce graph databases, Neo4j, Resource Description Framework, SPARQL, and Shapes Constraint Language as implementation choices tied to a question, data model, validation need, and operating environment.
staffSummary: Build M18 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Select an appropriate graph representation and validation approach for a bounded utility use case. The learner must leave with a usable graph implementation decision record, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: A team has a useful relationship map but has not decided how identities, queries, constraints, provenance, or system integration will work.
learnerDecision: Select an appropriate graph representation and validation approach for a bounded utility use case.
analogy: A street map, street address, route question, and building code serve different jobs. Graph tools also separate storage, identity, query, and validation.
learnerOutcomes: Explain The Machinery: GraphDB, Neo4j, RDF, SPARQL, SHACL in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish property graph, Resource Description Framework, triple, query, schema, constraint, and validation without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Keep product features and standards versions dated. Do not make a vendor choice before requirements, governance, scale, integration, and staff capability are clear.
Create a usable graph implementation decision record with evidence, roles, limits, review steps, and the next accountable action.
Defend the recommendation to Foundation, Practitioner, and Leader audiences while keeping disagreement and uncertainty visible.
curriculumOutcomes: Give The Machinery: GraphDB, Neo4j, RDF, SPARQL, SHACL one clear learning job inside Retrieval, Generation and the Data Foundation.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the graph implementation decision record.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.
Create an explicit bridge to the preceding and following modules without duplicating their work.
marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Select an appropriate graph representation and validation approach for a bounded utility use case.
Name the graph implementation decision record as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete graph implementation decision record, and names the next accountable action.
